items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: You had Buddy Johnson playing trombone. You had Dude playing drum.

ctx.x: Oh, about Eddie Vinson again, did he play a slide trombone always, or did he play the valve sometimes? He played slide. Always the slide.

You see, in 1908, he was playing with Pacific, him and Buddy. Buddy Johnson? Buddy Johnson, yeah. Buddy Johnson, yeah. See, in 1908, that's when he got in that Pacific band. Yeah. He took Frankie Duesen's job in that Pacific band. Eddie Vinson.
You know, what was that Pacific band? Was it the fellows that worked for the railroad or something there? No, no.

items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: Buddy Johnson and Lucie played with him a while.

ctx.x: Well, who was in Joel Lazard's band?

Well, a couple of fellas. Buddy Johnson and Lucie played with him a while. After he got, when he was young, he was the youngest one. And Frankie Doosen played with him a while. But that's two tramos they had. And George Sims was playing paratone. And another fella who played bass, he named George Stu, was a very bright fella. He was playing bass, drums. Now, the tuba, I don't know that fella was playing tuba. I don't know that fella was playing tuba. But he had a pretty good band, Joel Lazard's band. They called…

items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: I call him Buddy... he used to work at the... clothing place... he didn't name Buddy, he used to play alto.

ctx.x: And Johnny's brother, he was playing the baritone. He died afterwards. And then Connish, he died. Well, most of them, most of them, most of them, yes. And there were fellas playing alto, he died. Yeah, a fella played alto, I call him Buddy. He used to, the name Buddy, he used to work at the, at the, this, this clothing place right there, right on Connell Street there. What's he called? A clothing place? Yeah, he used to work, he used to work there. Oh, oh, wow. What'd you call that? Big clothing store. Yeah, on…
Joyce. Oh, Joyce, I don't know.
